# The required check set (#3971)
#
# WHAT THIS IS. The named list of check runs that decide whether a head SHA is
# reviewable. `required_check_state` (scripts/agents/lib/gh_project.sh) reads
# this file, matches the names EXACTLY against the check runs GitHub reports
# for a commit, and answers one of:
#
#   failed  - a required check on that head concluded failure. The head is the
#             developer's problem: `developer_submit_for_review.sh` refuses to
#             submit it, and `claude-code-review.yml` hands it back instead of
#             spending a review invocation relaying what the PR page already
#             shows.
#   pending - a required check is present and has not concluded. Nobody's
#             problem yet: the review trigger WAITS. A PR that is merely
#             mid-CI is never bounced back to the developer.
#   absent  - no required check is present on the head at all. Bounded grace
#             only (the checks have not been created yet); after it, treated
#             as clear.
#   clear   - every required check present on the head passed.
#
# WHY A NAMED LIST AND NOT "EVERY CHECK ON THE HEAD". Four of the checks on a
# PR head belong to the review itself (`head-gate`, `claude-review`,
# `head-not-reviewable`, `execute-review-decision`): gating on them deadlocks
# the gate against its own run -- `head-gate` cannot be complete at the moment
# `head-gate` decides. The rest of the not-required list is project bookkeeping — adding a card
# to the project board, stamping a lane, detecting a conflict. A flake in any
# of those must not be able to wedge the pipeline, and none of them says
# anything about whether the code is correct.
#
# ABSENT IS NOT PENDING. Most jobs below are path-filtered, so on any given PR
# most of them never run. A required check that is not attached to the head is
# not waited for and not counted against it — the path filter already decided
# it does not apply. This is what keeps the list safe to extend: naming a check
# here costs nothing on the PRs it does not run on.
#
# MAINTENANCE. Every job of every `pull_request`-triggered workflow must appear
# in exactly one of the two sections below — `tests/unit/test_required_checks.py`
# fails otherwise, in both directions (a name here that matches no job, and a
# job that this file never classified). A new smoke workflow therefore cannot
# be added without deciding whether it gates review.
#
# NAMES ARE CHECK-RUN NAMES, not job ids: a job with a `name:` reports under
# that name. `Install the working tree's formulas` is macos-brew-smoke.yml's
# `keg-install` job. The test above resolves both forms.

[required]
# Always runs on every PR (no path filter) — the presence signal the grace
# period keys on.
security-scan

# Quality gates for the paths they cover.
terraform-aws-validate
validate-web

# Smoke jobs. These are this project's executed-verification evidence (D-006);
# a red one is a real defect on the head, which is precisely what the developer
# round must fix rather than the reviewer relay.
claim-decision
The guard refuses the branch that holds the only copy
A merge that cannot be verified does not close its issue

# The round-state classification rules (#4015). Path-filtered, so it is free
# on the PRs it does not run for -- absent is not pending.
round-state-rules-hold

[not-required]
# The review's own runs, including the gate itself. Requiring any of them
# deadlocks the gate against itself: `claude-review` cannot be complete at the
# moment the gate decides whether to start `claude-review`, and `head-gate` is
# still running while it asks. (This is the deadlock Q-005 raises for the merge
# path; the merge path is untouched here.)
claude-review
head-gate
head-not-reviewable
execute-review-decision


# Project bookkeeping. None of these judges the code, and a flake in one must
# not hold a green PR out of review.
add-to-project
closure-hygiene
pr-hygiene
delete-abandoned-branch
link-revert-to-issue
stamp-closed-lane
detect
resolve
